note: Descriptions, pros, cons and maintenance notes are general industry guidance written for this app. Linked standards identify relevant documents; confirm the current edition and the grade your project needs with your supplier and a qualified professional.

materials.name: Plywood (MR / BWR grades)
materials.description: Cross-laminated wood veneers bonded with resin. The everyday workhorse for Indian carpentry: wardrobes, beds, TV units and kitchen carcasses.
cons: Interior (MR) grades swell if repeatedly wet
materials.maintenance: Keep edges sealed with edge-banding or laminate; wipe spills quickly in kitchens and bathrooms.

materials.name: Marine / BWP plywood
materials.description: Plywood made with boiling-water-proof bonding for repeated wet exposure. Common choice under sinks and in coastal homes.
pros: Best moisture tolerance among wood panels
Long service life when edges are sealed
cons: Fakes and mislabelled boards exist in the market
materials.maintenance: Seal all exposed edges and cut-outs; check the grade marking on every sheet at delivery.

materials.name: MDF (medium-density fibreboard)
materials.description: A dense, smooth board made from fine wood fibres and resin. Machines and paints beautifully for profiled shutters.
pros: Very smooth for paint and PU finishes
materials.maintenance: Keep away from standing water; use proper MDF screws and edge sealing.

materials.name: HDHMR board
materials.description: High-density, high-moisture-resistant fibreboard marketed in India as a step up from MDF for kitchens and wardrobes.
pros: Good moisture resistance for a fibreboard
cons: Still not a replacement for BWP plywood in constantly wet zones
materials.maintenance: Treat like MDF: seal edges and cut-outs; avoid continuous water contact.
materials.standardsNote: No specific BIS product standard for HDHMR was confirmed for this catalogue. Ask the manufacturer which standard and test results apply.

materials.name: Particle board
materials.description: Board made from wood chips and resin, mostly used in budget flat-pack furniture.
materials.maintenance: Keep dry; avoid repeated assembly and disassembly.

materials.name: Blockboard
materials.description: A core of solid wood strips sandwiched between veneers. Light and stiff over long spans.
pros: Lighter than plywood of the same thickness
materials.maintenance: Check for core gaps before buying; edge-band properly.

materials.name: Decorative laminates (HPL)
materials.description: Thin, hard-wearing sheets pressed onto boards. Thousands of colours, woodgrains, stones and textures.
cons: Visible dark edge lines on some grades
materials.maintenance: Wipe with a damp cloth and mild soap; avoid abrasive pads.

materials.name: Natural wood veneer
materials.description: Thin slices of real timber pressed onto boards and finished with PU or melamine polish.
pros: Authentic grain at lower cost than solid wood
cons: Finish quality depends on the polisher
materials.maintenance: Shield from harsh sunlight; dust with a soft cloth; re-polish every few years if worn.

materials.name: Acrylic finish
materials.description: High-gloss or matte acrylic sheets laminated onto boards for a seamless, mirror-like modern look.
materials.maintenance: Use microfibre cloth; avoid ammonia cleaners and scouring pads.

materials.name: PU paint and polish
materials.description: Polyurethane coatings sprayed on MDF or veneer for duco-style colour or clear, durable wood finishes.
materials.maintenance: Clean with soft cloth; touch-ups need the original painter or colour code.

materials.name: Granite
materials.description: Hard Indian natural stone, the classic kitchen platform material across the country.
materials.maintenance: Seal porous varieties; wipe oil and turmeric spills promptly.

materials.name: Engineered quartz
materials.description: Crushed quartz bound with resin into slabs with consistent colour and low porosity.
cons: Can scorch with very hot pans
materials.maintenance: Use trivets for hot vessels; clean with mild soap.
materials.standardsNote: Product standard not confirmed for this catalogue; ask the manufacturer for test certificates. Fabrication dust needs proper wet-cutting controls.

materials.name: Indian marble
materials.description: Classic Makrana-style whites, Udaipur greens and Ambaji varieties for floors, temples and feature walls.
cons: Etches with lemon, vinegar and some cleaners
materials.maintenance: Use pH-neutral cleaners; re-polish periodically; avoid acidic spills.

materials.name: Sandstone
materials.description: Warm-toned Rajasthani stone used for jaali, cladding, courtyards and outdoor floors.
materials.maintenance: Seal against stains; clean with soft brushes, not acid.

materials.name: Kota stone
materials.description: Dense blue-green or brown limestone from Rajasthan, loved for durable, cool, low-cost floors.
pros: Can be polished to a soft sheen
materials.maintenance: Mop with plain water or neutral cleaner; re-polish to restore sheen.

materials.name: Terrazzo
materials.description: Chips of marble or glass set in cement or resin and ground smooth — a Mumbai Art Deco favourite returning in modern homes.
pros: Durable and seamless when cast in situ
cons: Cracks can show if base moves
materials.maintenance: Seal after grinding; clean with neutral cleaners.

materials.name: Terracotta tiles
materials.description: Fired clay tiles with warm earthy tones, used across Kerala, Goa and Bengal.
materials.maintenance: Seal regularly; avoid harsh acids.

materials.name: Athangudi tiles
materials.description: Hand-made cement tiles from the Chettinad village of Athangudi, cast on glass and sun-cured, in vivid patterns.
materials.maintenance: Mop with plain water and a mild coconut-oil based polish as recommended by makers.

materials.name: Ceramic tiles
materials.description: Glazed clay tiles for walls and light-traffic floors, especially kitchens and bathrooms.
cons: Less durable than vitrified for heavy floor use
materials.maintenance: Clean grout lines periodically; reseal grout in wet areas.

materials.name: Vitrified tiles (GVT, PGVT, double charge)
materials.description: Dense, low-absorption tiles that are India's most common modern flooring choice.
cons: Polished finishes can be slippery when wet
materials.maintenance: Mop with neutral cleaner; choose matt or anti-skid in wet zones.

materials.name: Red oxide (cement) floor
materials.description: Cement flooring coloured with red oxide pigment and burnished by hand — the cool, glossy floor of old Kerala, Tamil and Bengal homes.
materials.maintenance: Mop with plain water; occasional wax polish keeps the sheen.

materials.name: Solid wood (teak, sheesham, mango)
materials.description: Seasoned hardwood for carved doors, heirloom furniture and pooja mandirs.
cons: Moves with humidity if not seasoned
materials.maintenance: Polish every few years; keep humidity steady; buy seasoned, legally sourced timber.

materials.name: Engineered wood flooring
materials.description: A real hardwood top layer over a stable multi-ply base — a wood floor that copes better with Indian humidity.
pros: More stable than solid wood planks
cons: Not for bathrooms or wet kitchens
materials.maintenance: Dry mop; felt pads under furniture; avoid wet mopping.

materials.name: Laminate flooring
materials.description: A photographic wood or stone layer on HDF core, clicked together over an underlay.
cons: Swells if water seeps into joints
materials.maintenance: Dry or damp-mop only; wipe spills immediately.

materials.name: Cane and rattan
materials.description: Woven natural palm stems used for chairs, shutters, partitions and lamp shades.
materials.maintenance: Vacuum gently; occasional damp wipe; keep out of strong sun.

materials.name: Aluminium sections
materials.description: Extruded aluminium for sliding windows, slim partitions, profile shutters and kitchen frames.
materials.maintenance: Clean tracks; lubricate rollers; check gaskets before monsoon.

materials.name: uPVC windows and doors
materials.description: Plastic-profile windows with steel reinforcement, popular for sound and dust sealing in Indian cities.
pros: Good sealing against dust and noise
cons: Quality depends on profile and fabricator
materials.maintenance: Clean drainage slots before monsoon; keep hardware lubricated.

materials.name: Glass (toughened and laminated)
materials.description: Safety glass for shower enclosures, partitions, railings and table tops.
pros: Safety glass breaks more safely than ordinary glass
cons: Must be the right safety type for the location
materials.maintenance: Squeegee shower glass after use; check hardware and seals yearly.

materials.name: Gypsum board false ceilings
materials.description: Gypsum plasterboard on metal framing, the standard for modern false ceilings and cove lighting.
cons: Needs moisture-resistant boards in wet areas
materials.maintenance: Fix roof or AC leaks immediately; repaint periodically.

materials.name: Acrylic emulsion paint
materials.description: Water-based interior paints in matt to sheen finishes — the default for Indian walls.
materials.maintenance: Use washable grades in kids' rooms and kitchens; repaint every few years.

materials.name: Lime plaster and lime wash
materials.description: Traditional breathable plasters and washes with soft, cloudy texture — revived for heritage and eco homes.
uses: Bathrooms with traditional finishes such as tadelakt-style work
materials.maintenance: Re-wash periodically; avoid plastic paints over lime.

materials.name: Microcement and cement textures
materials.description: Thin cement-based coatings for seamless walls, floors and furniture with an industrial feel.
pros: Works over existing tiles when specified
materials.maintenance: Reseal as advised; avoid harsh cleaners.

materials.name: Wallpaper and wall coverings
materials.description: Printed paper, vinyl and fabric coverings for feature walls and rentals.
materials.maintenance: Choose washable vinyl in high-touch areas; fix damp first.

materials.name: Waterproofing systems
materials.description: Cementitious, polyurethane or membrane systems under tiles in bathrooms, balconies and terraces.
cons: Invisible once tiled, so workmanship is hard to check
materials.maintenance: Ask for a pond (flood) test before tiling; maintain grout and joints.
materials.standardsNote: Product standards depend on the system chosen. Ask the applicator for the specification and warranty terms.

materials.name: Acrylic solid surface
materials.description: Non-porous acrylic sheet that can be joined invisibly and thermoformed into curves.
cons: Heat marks from very hot pans
materials.maintenance: Clean with mild abrasive cream; scratches can be buffed out.

materials.name: Brass hardware and accents
materials.description: Handles, hinges, inlays and lamps in brass — a signature of Indian craft from Moradabad and beyond.
materials.maintenance: Lacquered brass: damp cloth only. Unlacquered: polish as desired.

materials.name: Hinges, channels and fittings
materials.description: Soft-close hinges, drawer channels, tandem boxes, corner solutions and lift-up systems for modular storage.
materials.maintenance: Clean channels; re-align hinges yearly; avoid overloading drawers.

materials.name: Sanitaryware and CP fittings
materials.description: WCs, basins, mixers, showers and concealed cisterns for Indian bathrooms.
materials.maintenance: Descale aerators and shower heads; keep access panels for concealed cisterns.
materials.standardsNote: Many sanitaryware and fitting standards exist; confirm the applicable ones with your plumber or supplier.

materials.name: Flush door shutters
materials.description: Factory-made doors with a solid or blockboard core, faced with veneer or laminate.
cons: Bathroom doors need water-resistant cores and edge protection
materials.maintenance: Protect bottom edges in wet areas; adjust hinges as they settle.
